folder_html:
LIVE CHLOROPHYLL / ALGAL ACTIVITY

Chlorophyll-a concentration at the lake surface, a proxy for phytoplankton abundance/biomass. NOT a toxin measurement and NOT a harmful-algal-bloom diagnosis.

Chlorophyll-a concentration (mg/m^3), logarithmic (base-10) scale: LOWEST 0.079 (dark blue) → common 1.73 (green/yellow) → HIGHEST+ 99.93 (deep purple). Equal color per decade of concentration (ocean-color standard); displayed values are true concentrations, never altered. High values indicate biomass/activity, not toxins.

Units: mg/m^3
Source: NOAA CoastWatch S-NPP+NOAA-20 VIIRS chlorophyll-a NRT gapfilled Daily (ERDDAP nesdisVHNnoaaSNPPnoaa20NRTchlaGapfilledDaily), fallback SQ Daily (nesdisVHNSQchlaDaily)
Update: daily composites
Data time: 2026-10-01 08:00 AM EDT (7-day median mosaic)
Processed: 2026-10-03 01:58 PM EDT
Why high values turn red/purple: Very high values (blooms, algal activity, turbid intrusions) compress into red-violet/deep-purple; common background concentrations own most of the color resolution.
Provenance: ERDDAP dataset
